Extract qCMDE/IWMDE Density Diagnostics

Source: R/density-diagnostics.R
density_diagnostics.Rd

Extracts the compact reliability diagnostics attached to a qCMDE/IWMDE hypothesis result. The diagnostics describe the posterior ordinate computation. They do not include uncertainty in the prior ordinate or, for IWMDE, uncertainty from estimating its conditional weight function.

Usage

density_diagnostics(object, ...)

Arguments

object

an object returned by hypothesis() with density_method = "qCMDE" or density_method = "IWMDE", or an RoBMA_density_ordinate_error caught from a failed or rejected point-ordinate computation.

...

unused.

Value

A data frame of class RoBMA_density_diagnostics, with one row per computed or failed requested point ordinate. Columns identify the estimator, parameter, requested and evaluated values, schema/source provenance, row counts, active mass, relative MCSE, ESS, largest contribution share, finite terms, normalization, truncation, and quadrature checks, the qCMDE pilot-gate columns (the nested normalization grids have no refinement sequence to stop, so pilot_gate_stopped is FALSE and pilot_bulk_ess is NA), fixed-sampling state, policy thresholds, weight fallbacks, status, and warnings.

The exact columns, in order, are schema_version, algorithm_version, source_fingerprint, estimator, internal_method, working_distribution, normalization_basis, ordered_error_status, block_numerator_relative_error, block_denominator_relative_error, block_max_order, block_max_panels, block_native_nodes, density_method, parameter, level, requested_value, evaluation_value, requested_samples, achieved_row_budget, eligible_rows, evaluated_rows, finite_terms, active_mass, relative_mcse, active_branch_relative_mcse, active_mass_relative_mcse, mixture_mcse_type, sampling_relative_mcse, sampling_fraction, mcmc_uncertainty_scope, sampling_uncertainty_type, ess, max_weight_share, normalization_relative_error, stability_metric, stability_relative_error, ordinate_relative_change, lattice_resolution_relative_error, normalization_truncation, normalization_truncation_status, truncation_ordinate_bound, quadrature_relative_change, pilot_gate_stopped, pilot_bulk_ess, target_relative_mcse, stability_warning_threshold, stability_rejection_threshold, quadrature_warning_threshold, quadrature_rejection_threshold, warning_relative_mcse, warning_min_finite_terms, warning_min_ess, warning_max_weight_share, all_rows_used, target_met, precision_target_met, sampling_target_met, bf_grade_met, n_weight_fallbacks, weight_fallback_reasons, status, ordinate, log_ordinate, numerical_status, failure_reason, and warnings.

Details

Point ordinates evaluate one fixed posterior-row sample whose size is chosen by samples before any ordinate contributions are computed. Precision, effective-sample-size, and contribution-concentration diagnostics never determine whether that finite estimate is returned. An unmet target_relative_mcse produces a warning; increase samples or set it to Inf to use every eligible row. The table records the requested and achieved sample sizes, all_rows_used, whether the precision target was met, and whether the ordinate passed the independent numerical-stability gates. Finite row budgets use a reproducible simple random sample without replacement. For a purely continuous ordinate, relative_mcse and ess describe the selected continuous posterior-row sequence. For a mixed point/continuous ordinate evaluated on every active continuous row, they use the full conditioned-chain sequence, with zero contributions for inactive rows, and therefore include active-mass uncertainty and its covariance with continuous contributions. With a subset of active rows, active_branch_relative_mcse describes the selected active-row contribution sequence and active_mass_relative_mcse comes from the complete binary indicator chain. relative_mcse is their conservative worst-correlation delta upper bound on the unconditional density scale. It is suitable as a descriptive precision diagnostic but does not certify the unobserved full-mixture covariance, so bf_grade_met remains false. sampling_relative_mcse separately reports the finite-population simple-random-sampling component conditional on the fitted rows (sampling_uncertainty_type = "finite_population_srswor"). The sampling design is exact, but the standard error is an estimate: the usual without-replacement formula applied to the sample variance of the selected contributions, and zero when every eligible row is used. It is not added to the selected-row sequence MCSE, which already describes the actual selected estimator sequence.

These fields concern the continuous density ordinate. At a location that is also a posterior atom, the atom probability remains a separate discrete mass and is never added to the density ordinate.

ordinate and log_ordinate describe the posterior density at the requested point, not the model's marginal likelihood. log_ordinate is retained only when actually computed; it is not reconstructed for older results. numerical_status distinguishes finite, underflow, overflow, arithmetic_failure, invalid_density, zero_without_log_evidence, nonfinite, and not_computed. Underflow/overflow requires finite log evidence and confirmation that exponentiating that log loses range. A zero without this evidence is not classified as a mathematical zero. A small density alone does not establish unreliability.

Failed requested points retain separate diagnostic records with a failure_reason, including failures occurring before a final ordinate was obtained. status = "unavailable" distinguishes these failures from a finite positive ordinate rejected by accuracy diagnostics. Ordinary-scale precision diagnostics lost to underflow/overflow are unavailable, not zero error or proof of convergence. Retaining a log estimate does not authorize a Bayes factor: the existing finite-positive ordinate requirement is unchanged. Legacy tables remain inspectable with unknown new fields set to NA. A hypothesis result without attached diagnostics, such as one whose point ordinates were estimated with density_method = "KDE" or one without a point hypothesis, stops with the class RoBMA_density_diagnostics_unavailable. Density ordinate, diagnostic-unavailable, plot, and construction (RoBMA_density_construction_error) conditions share the RoBMA_density_error parent while retaining their specific condition classes.

The reliability policy warns when relative MCSE is at least 5 percent, ESS is below 100, the largest contribution share is at least 20 percent, or fewer than 100 finite contributions remain. These same-sample diagnostics do not reject a finite fixed-design estimate. Their warning thresholds are returned as columns rather than being implicit. For a descriptive mixed density curve using the conservative partial-row bound, a finite ESS below the usual curve rejection threshold is retained as a warning when the quantitative mixture-scale MCSE checks pass.

qCMDE's full method diagnostics distinguish pilot_normalization_integral from final_normalization_integral; IWMDE uses support_grid_normalization_integral. This compact accessor reports the relative difference of the final integral from the active mass as normalization_relative_error. For qCMDE it is a bookkeeping check, not a discretization error: rows normalized on the lattice are normalized by the same trapezoid rule, on the same grid, that integrates them, so they sum to the active mass up to roundoff by construction, and rows normalized in closed form contribute their analytic mass within the range. The discretization and truncation errors of the lattice normalizers are reported by ordinate_relative_change, lattice_resolution_relative_error, and truncation_ordinate_bound. The active policy check is identified by stability_metric: qCMDE checks its posterior ordinate error estimate (ordinate_error_estimate), whereas IWMDE checks normalization mass. The qCMDE estimate adds three parts. ordinate_relative_change is the ordinate's movement between the selected normalization grid and the coarser nested grid over the same range. It estimates the discretization error of the lattice normalizers; it is an estimate, not a bound, because a row narrower than the lattice step can escape both grids alike. Rows whose lattice normalization is under-resolved also contribute an ordinate-share weighted resolution estimate (lattice_resolution_relative_error), using the kernel width or nested-grid log curvature at each row's maximum. This component and their sum are estimates, not rigorous bounds: a sharp prior core can be narrower than its likelihood kernel. Rows whose Gaussian likelihood kernel meets a normal prior are normalized by the closed-form mass of their support when their evaluated values are those of that closed form: their normalizer is the same on every grid, so they add no discretization change, lattice-resolution component or truncation. truncation_ordinate_bound is \(t / (1 - t)\) for the largest fraction \(t\) of any row's conditional mass outside the normalization range (normalization_truncation): a row normalizer missing that fraction overstates the row's density by at most this relative amount. normalization_truncation_status states how \(t\) is known: "exact" for rows whose Gaussian likelihood kernel meets a normal prior, "bound" for a Gaussian kernel with another proper prior, and "estimate" (from the exponential envelope of the tails at the range ends) otherwise; it reports the weakest status among the rows. The range covers every row's central normalization_prob interval, so \(t\) is at most 1 - normalization_prob (for estimated rows, as estimated once their extension reaches its target) and truncation_ordinate_bound is at most (1 - normalization_prob) / normalization_prob, about 0.1 percent at the default 0.999. The extension of an estimated row stops at its limit (four initial range widths per side and 40 passes), at a value the joint density cannot evaluate, or for a tail that does not decay; the reported normalization_truncation and truncation_ordinate_bound can then exceed these values. Setting normalization_prob closer to 1 widens the range and lowers the truncation; increasing normalization_points refines the grid. The table also reports the stability and adaptive-quadrature warning/rejection thresholds.

Ordered effects use normalized conditional-source contributions for both requested methods. Regular exact offsets can use a positive total/share block. The complete numerical ratio error must be at most 0.025 for every evaluated row, separately from the MCMC precision diagnostics. The columns internal_method, working_distribution, and normalization_basis identify this computation while estimator retains the requested method. ordered_error_status preserves its estimated error status. Block numerator and denominator errors, maximum quadrature order/panel count, and actual native normalizer node count are reported in the block_* columns. Exact offsets classified as nonfinite or unsupported are excluded only from density curves; explicit point requests retain their structural or precision refusal. The ordered per-row limit of 0.025 is separate from the generic stability warning/rejection thresholds reported in this table. Source-normalization refusals have class RoBMA_ordered_normalization_error and retain iwmde_ordered_normalization_error as a compatibility ancestor. Their condition's proof field contains the numerical integration evidence. When only some ordered evaluations lack certified contribution variation, their MCMC error and ESS stay unavailable while other evaluations retain their metrics. A printed table footnote reports the partial uncertainty status and its reason; the original selected-row scope stays in its column. Such curves fail the MCMC availability gate, and an affected point cannot meet its precision target. If every evaluation is affected, the full unavailable scope is retained. A finite log MCSE whose absolute value underflows remains a separate representation limitation.

See also

hypothesis()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
result <- hypothesis(
  fit,
  hypothesis = "mu != 0 vs mu = 0"
)
density_diagnostics(result)

failed <- tryCatch(
  hypothesis(
    fit,
    hypothesis     = "mu != 0 vs mu = 0",
    density_method = "IWMDE"
  ),
  RoBMA_density_ordinate_error = identity
)
density_diagnostics(failed)
} # }
